data.gender_notes: Hagai is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Hagai means ‘joyful’ or ‘exalted’. This name appears in the Old Testament as the name of a prophet who delivered God’s message to the returning exiles in Jerusalem. It is also a name of praise and celebration. The name Hagai carries the meaning “Joyful, Exalted” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Hagai usually hope their child will grow to embody joyful, exalted and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embrace joy and exaltation in your spiritual journey.
data.etymology: Hagai belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Joyful, Exalted.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hagai total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Hagai is rooted in ancient Jewish history and culture as it appears in the Old Testament. It symbolizes the joy and excitement that the returning exiles felt when they came back to their homeland after years of exile. The name Hagai is a reminder of the rich history and cultural heritage of the Jewish people.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Hagai is rooted in its meaning of ‘joyful’ or ‘exalted’. It reminds us of the joy that comes from being in God's presence and following His will. It also reminds us of the exalted state that we can achieve when we live our lives in accordance with God's plan for us. The name Hagai encourages us to live joyfully and to exalt God in all that we do.
